h-niyya.n: Intention turns habit into worship: work, study and spending on one's family are all rewarded through intention.

h-qulub.n: The measure of worth before Allah is the heart and deeds, not appearance, wealth or social standing.

h-ridallah.n: A cure for pleasing people at the expense of principle: whoever puts Allah's pleasure first, Allah suffices him against people.

h-khafi.n: Being hidden and not seeking to be seen is a beloved quality, in an age when people measure themselves by their number of followers.

h-ghadab-julus.n: A practical, physical remedy: changing your body's position breaks the surge of anger and keeps you from rash action.

h-ghadab-istiadha.n: Seeking refuge with Allah is the first thing to say when angry.

h-ghadab-sukut.n: What people regret most in anger is what they said; temporary silence protects the relationship.

h-kazm.n: Restraining anger is worth the most when you are able to take revenge.

h-rifq.n: Gentleness is not weakness but a more successful way of reaching the result.

h-rifq-zana.n: The Prophet ﷺ said it to ‘A'ishah when she rode a difficult camel and kept pulling it back and forth; gentleness even with animals.

h-muflis-tabbaan.n: Even in a dispute, the believer's tongue stays clean.

h-afw-izz.n: People fear their forgiveness will be seen as weakness, so the promise came: forgiveness increases honour, it does not reduce it.

h-zulm-zulumat.n: A warning to the wrongdoer and a consolation for the wronged.

h-dawat-mazlum.r: Ibn ‘Abbas (from the Prophet's ﷺ advice to Mu‘adh)
h-dawat-mazlum.n: The wronged have a weapon that is never blocked, and those with power have a stern warning.

h-unsur.n: Helping a friend who is doing wrong means stopping him from it, not backing him in it.

h-muflis.n: People's rights are not cancelled by acts of worship, and the wronged never lose their right.

h-la-darar.n: A major legal maxim: harm may not be initiated, nor answered with greater harm — a basis for refusing ongoing abuse.

h-la-yuldagh.n: Forgiveness does not mean naivety; the believer learns from experience and sets boundaries that protect him from being hurt again.

h-yuhibbu.n: The deepest cure for envy: wishing for others what you wish for yourself.

h-la-tahasadu.n: A list of what ruins brotherhood: envy, hatred, turning one's back, and unfair competition.

h-hasad-ithnatayn.n: “Envy” here means healthy emulation: wishing for a blessing like someone else's without wanting it taken from them, and only in matters of good.

h-hajr-thalath.n: Estrangement has a time limit, and the better person is the one who greets first, not the one who waits.

h-istalaha.n: Grudges delay forgiveness; reconciliation is not a social courtesy but an act of worship.

h-islah.n: “The shaver”: it shaves away religion as a razor shaves hair, so mending relationships is among the highest acts of devotion.

h-mira.n: Give up fruitless arguing even when you are right: winning a debate is not always a win for the relationship.

h-afshu-salam.n: Greeting with peace is the simplest key to breaking the ice and building affection.

h-akhbirhu.n: Expressing positive feelings is a Sunnah, not a weakness.

h-khalil.n: A friend reshapes you without you noticing, so choosing your company is a decisive decision.

h-jalis.n: You benefit from a good companion in every case, and are harmed by a bad one in every case, even if you do not act like him.

h-maa-man-ahabb.r: Anas ibn Malik and Ibn Mas‘ud
h-maa-man-ahabb.n: Loving the righteous raises you to them, even if your deeds fall short.

h-yashkur-nas.n: Thanking people is part of thanking Allah.

h-kafiuhu.n: Supplication is the repayment of one who has nothing else to give.

h-ghiba.n: Backbiting is mentioning a real fault, and slander is mentioning a fault that does not exist; both are forbidden.

h-yaqul-khayran.n: A simple test before speaking: is it good? If not, then silence.

h-kalima.n: A passing word may be the heaviest thing on the scale.

h-muslim-salima.n: A practical definition of Islam: people being safe from your harm.

h-zann.n: Bad suspicion presents itself as “intuition”, and the Prophet ﷺ called it the most false of speech.

h-kalima-tayyiba.n: Whoever has no money still has a good word to give in charity.

h-sitr.n: Doors that multiply: relieving, easing and concealing — and the reward is of the same kind as the deed.

h-mujahirin.n: Whoever falls into sin should stay under Allah's cover and not expose himself, and repent between himself and his Lord.

h-munafiq.n: Three practical signs for testing trust — in others and in oneself.

h-da-ma-yaribuk.n: When unsure, choose what the heart is at peace with; truthfulness is peace of mind before it is a duty.

h-birr-ithm.n: An inner compass: what you would hate for people to find out usually has something wrong in it.

h-mustashar.n: Whoever is consulted must advise honestly, and whoever seeks advice should choose someone trustworthy.

h-atqan.n: Doing work well is worship, even if no one is watching you.

h-ajir.n: The worker's right to his wage straight away, without delay.

h-kullukum-rai.n: Everyone is responsible within their own circle: father, mother, manager and employee.

h-ada-dayn.n: A sincere intention to repay brings Allah's help in settling the debt.

h-matl.n: Delaying someone's due when you are able to pay is plain injustice.

h-samh.n: Easygoing generosity, even when claiming what you are owed.

h-inzar.n: Giving a struggling debtor more time, or letting the debt go, is a deed of great reward.

h-ghina-nafs.n: True richness is a feeling of sufficiency, not a number in an account.

h-kafaf.n: Success does not require wealth: Islam, sufficiency and contentment.

h-amin-sirbih.n: Redefining blessing: safety, good health and today's food are the whole of “this world”.

h-unzuru-asfal.n: A precise psychological rule: the direction of comparison decides how blessed you feel; in matters of religion, look to those above you.

h-tawakkul-tayr.n: The birds “go out in the morning” — they leave and search; true trust in Allah includes effort along with a calm heart.

h-iqilha.n: Trusting Allah does not mean abandoning the means; take every means, then leave the result to Allah.

h-hatab.n: There is no shame in humble work; dignity lies in lawful earning, however modest.

h-kafil-yatim.n: Caring for an orphan raises a person to be beside the Prophet ﷺ.

h-armala.n: Serving the weak equals the greatest acts of worship.

h-la-tahqiranna.n: The smallest kindness has value — a practical way in for anyone who feels unable to do good.

h-anfauhum.n: For whoever feels they have lost meaning, benefiting people is a wide door to regaining it.

h-khayrukum-ahlih.n: True character is measured inside the home, not outside it.

h-akmal-iman.n: The perfection of faith is linked to treating one's wife well.

h-la-yafrak.n: A balanced view: do not judge your partner by one fault and forget the good. It applies to both spouses.

h-istawsu.n: A repeated Prophetic instruction to treat women well.

h-radiya-ghadba.n: The Prophet's ﷺ attention to the subtlest signs of his wife's feelings, and his calm handling of her anger without escalation.

h-mataa.n: A righteous wife is the greatest blessing of this world.

h-dhat-din.n: The criterion for choosing: religion and character are the foundation, without neglecting other considerations.

h-tardawna.n: Guidance for families: do not make marriage difficult with exaggerated material standards.

h-shabab.n: Practical solutions for desire: marriage when able, and fasting when not.

h-thalatha-awn.n: Whoever seeks marriage with the intention of chastity, Allah will help him.

h-rughm.n: Parents' old age is a golden opportunity for Paradise, not only a burden.

h-rida-walid.n: Honouring parents is a direct path to Allah's pleasure, in anything other than disobedience to Him.

h-asma-umm.n: A difference in religion or practice does not cancel the duty of kindness and keeping ties.

h-sila-rizq.n: Keeping ties of kinship brings blessing in provision and lifespan.

h-mal.n: Whoever keeps ties with relatives who are cold to him has a supporter from Allah, and the sin is on them, not him.

h-adl-awlad.n: Favouring one child over another in giving plants enmity between them.

h-yarham-saghir.n: Mercy towards the young and respect for the old, together.

h-rahimun.n: Mercy towards creation is a path to the Creator's mercy.

h-walad-salih.n: Honouring parents does not end with death: your supplication and charity on their behalf reach them.

h-kalima-lil-ahl.n: Even a morsel you give your wife is charity with the right intention; spending on family is worship.

h-ajaban.n: The believer gains in every situation: through gratitude in blessing and patience in hardship.

h-nasab.r: Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri and Abu Hurayrah
h-nasab.n: Even worry and emotional sadness — not only physical pain — carry reward and expiation.

h-ashadd-bala.n: Severe trial is not a sign of anger; it may even be a sign of rank.

h-azam-jaza.n: Your stance towards the trial (acceptance or resentment) is what decides its fruit.

h-maradh-kutib.n: Illness does not cut off the reward of your usual worship, so do not grieve over what illness keeps you from.

h-dawa.n: Hope of a cure is part of faith, and searching for it is taking the means.

h-tadawaw.n: Seeking treatment is commanded, including mental health care; seeing a doctor does not contradict trust in Allah.

h-habibatayn.n: Losing a precious sense, met with patience, is compensated with Paradise.

h-la-yatamanna.n: A clear prohibition of wishing for death because of pain, directing heavy feelings into a supplication that leaves the matter to Allah.

h-yurid-khayran.n: A calamity may be a door to good that Allah intended for you.

h-sabr-diya.n: Patience is “radiance” — light that carries heat and hardship — unlike prayer, which is pure “light”.

h-yatasabbar.n: Patience is a skill gained by practice: whoever strives for it, Allah helps him with it.

h-hamm.w: Morning, evening and in times of worry
h-hamm.n: Worry is about the future and sadness about the past; this supplication covers eight doors of human weakness.

h-karb.n: The supplication of distress: the Prophet ﷺ used to say it in times of hardship.

h-dhunnun.n: Declaring Allah's oneness, glorifying Him and admitting one's fault: three keys to relief.

h-abduk.n: A supplication that combines surrender to Allah's decree with asking that the Quran be the cure for sadness.

h-rahmataka.w: In hardship and when affairs are scattered
h-rahmataka.n: Asking Allah not to leave you to yourself even for a moment, and to set right “all” your affairs.

h-hasbuna.n: The great words of entrusting when afraid of people or of the future.

h-bismillah-yadurr.n: A daily protective remembrance that calms an anxious heart.

h-ruqya-alam.n: A Prophetic ruqyah the sick person recites over himself.

h-adhhib-bas.w: For the sick and those who visit them
h-adhhib-bas.n: The Prophet ﷺ used to seek protection with it for members of his family.

h-la-bas.n: A Prophetic word of comfort that makes illness a purification, not a punishment.

h-ayn-haqq.n: An affirmation of the evil eye, while forbidding excessive fear of it or explaining everything by it.

h-barrakt.r: Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf
h-barrakt.n: Preventing the evil eye on the side of the one who looks: saying “May Allah bless it for you” when something impresses him.

h-muawwidhat.n: The last two surahs are the greatest protection.

h-uidhukuma.n: Protecting children through remembrance of Allah.

h-khattaun.n: Making mistakes is human nature; excellence lies in returning quickly.

h-farah-tawba.n: Allah does not only accept your repentance; He rejoices at it — an image that breaks despair over sin.

h-yabsut-yadah.n: The door of repentance is open at every hour.

h-ma-daawtani.n: No sin is greater than Allah's forgiveness for the one who calls on Him and hopes in Him.

h-sayyid-istighfar.w: Morning, evening and after a sin
h-sayyid-istighfar.n: Whoever says it during the day with conviction and dies that day is among the people of Paradise.

h-atbi-sayyia.r: Abu Dharr and Mu‘adh ibn Jabal
h-atbi-sayyia.n: A practical method: do not wait for perfection; follow every bad deed with a good one.

h-qatil-mia.n: No sin closes the door of repentance, and changing one's environment is a key part of change.

h-waswasa-sarih.n: Hating the whispers and finding them monstrous is a sign of faith, not of disbelief.

h-tajawaz.n: Thoughts that pass through the mind without action or speech are not held against you by Allah.

h-waswasa-intahi.n: The cure for whisperings: seek refuge, then stop following the thought — do not argue with it.

h-muqallib.w: Always, and when faith feels weak
h-muqallib.n: Even the Prophet ﷺ asked for steadfastness; the heart's fluctuation is natural, and supplication is its cure.

h-ahdini.n: A short, comprehensive supplication for every decision or task.

h-taqwaha.n: Purifying the self by seeking Allah's help, not by one's own strength alone.

h-kfini-halal.w: For paying off debt and wider provision
h-kfini-halal.n: The Prophet ﷺ taught it to a man unable to pay what he owed, and said: even if you had a debt like a mountain, Allah would pay it for you.

h-la-sahl.w: Before an exam or a hard task
h-la-sahl.n: A supplication for making the difficult easy: exams and heavy tasks.

h-zawal-nima.w: When afraid of losing a blessing
h-zawal-nima.n: Seeking refuge to preserve the blessings you have.

h-istijaba-ajal.n: Impatience and giving up supplication are the biggest barriers to a response.

h-nuzul.n: A daily open appointment with Allah in the last part of the night.

h-sujud.n: Prostration is the closest moment, so place your worries in it.

h-hazabahu.n: Prayer is the first refuge the believer turns to when something important happens.

h-arihna.n: Prayer is rest from tiredness, not a tiredness to rest from.

h-din-yusr.n: Being too hard on yourself ends in giving up; “aim for what is right, and if you cannot reach it, come close”.

h-adwamuha.n: Keeping up a little is more beneficial than temporary enthusiasm for a lot — the principle of building habits.

h-haqq-nafs.r: Abu Juhayfah (Salman said it to Abu al-Darda', and the Prophet ﷺ confirmed it)
h-haqq-nafs.n: Balance between worship, oneself, family and work.

h-nimatan.n: Most people lose out in how they invest their health and free time.

h-ightanim.n: A life plan in brief: every present blessing is an opportunity before it changes.

h-muamin-qawi.n: A complete method: eagerness + seeking help + no helplessness before the event, and contentment and leaving “if only” after it.

h-ihfadh.n: In Ahmad's narration: “Know that victory comes with patience, relief with distress, and with hardship comes ease.” A root cure for the fear of people.

h-yassiru.n: A rule for upbringing, leadership and calling to good.

h-ihsan.n: Excellence is required in every deed, even in the hardest situations.

h-makarim.n: Good character is the aim of the message, not its margin.

h-ahsanukum-khuluqan.n: Good character is the path to being close to the Prophet ﷺ in the Hereafter.

h-kibr.n: A precise definition of arrogance: rejecting the truth and looking down on people; it has nothing to do with a good appearance.

h-tawadau.n: Humility prevents two things: boasting and transgression.

h-nasiha.n: Sincere advice means wanting good for the person advised, and it is given gently and privately.

h-munkar.n: Levels of opposing wrong according to ability, taking care that opposing it does not lead to a greater wrong.

h-sabaa-yuzilluhum.n: Resisting desire at the height of temptation raises a person to the shade of the Throne.

h-man-taraka.r: A man from the desert, from the Prophet ﷺ
h-man-taraka.n: Leaving something forbidden, or a forbidden relationship, is not a loss: Allah's replacement is greater.

h-hayaa.n: Modesty is a trait that protects its owner, and does not mean a shyness that holds one back from the truth.
